note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What does a permanent wave (perm) do to the hair?
options: It coats each hair with a strong film that holds the curl in place
It adds new protein at the root so the hair grows out curly
It dries the hair into a curl that lasts until the next shampoo
It breaks and re-forms bonds inside the hair to give a new shape

questions.stem: Which bonds inside the hair does the waving lotion break, so that the hair can take the shape of the rod?
options: Disulphide bonds
Bonds in the hair's natural oil
Bonds between the hair and the scalp
Bonds in the melanin (colour) only

questions.stem: What is the main job of the neutraliser in a perm?
options: To soften the hair so that the rods slide out more easily
To re-join the broken bonds so the new shape is fixed
To put back colour that the waving lotion took out
To speed up the waving lotion so it works faster

questions.stem: What is the main active ingredient in many alkaline (cold) waving lotions?
options: Ammonium thioglycolate
Hydrogen peroxide
Sodium hydroxide
Sodium chloride (table salt)

questions.stem: How does an acid (acid-balanced) perm usually compare with an alkaline perm?
options: It gives a tighter curl and suits very resistant hair best
It needs no neutraliser, because the acid fixes the curl
It is safe to use on hair that was relaxed with a hydroxide relaxer
It gives a softer curl and is gentler on fragile or tinted hair

questions.stem: Why do you check the porosity of the hair (how easily it takes in liquid) before a perm?
options: Porous hair resists lotion, so it always needs the strongest lotion
Porosity tells you what colour rods and end papers to use
Porous hair takes in lotion fast, so a milder lotion may be needed
Porosity only matters for hair colour, not for perming the hair

questions.stem: How do you test the elasticity of the hair?
options: Pull a small handful of hair hard to see whether it comes out at the root
Gently stretch one wet hair and see if it springs back without breaking
Rub a strand between your fingers to feel how rough the cuticle is
Hold a strand up to the light and check how much it shines and reflects

questions.stem: Marcia has small open cuts on her scalp from scratching. What should you do about her perm?
options: Put barrier cream over the cuts and carry on with the perm
Use an acid perm instead, because it will not sting the cuts
Do not perm today, and book her back when her scalp has healed
Perm only the sections of hair that are well away from the cuts

questions.stem: Kadian's hair was relaxed with a sodium hydroxide (lye) relaxer. Why should it not be given a thio perm?
options: The relaxer makes the hair take the curl too quickly and too tightly
The perm would wash the relaxer out and make the hair revert
The rods cannot grip relaxed hair, so the curl will drop
The two chemicals do not work together and can break the hair

questions.stem: What is a pre-perm test curl used for?
options: To check whether the client's skin is allergic to the neutraliser
To remove product build-up from the hair before wrapping
To soften the hair so that it is easier to wrap
To see how the hair takes the lotion and how long it may need

questions.stem: The maker of a perm lotion asks for a skin test. When should it be done?
options: Straight after the perm is finished, while the hair is still wet
Halfway through processing, on a small patch at the back of the neck
Before the service, as early as the maker's instructions say
Only once the client says her scalp is starting to feel itchy

questions.stem: Why must the stylist wear gloves when applying waving lotion and neutraliser?
options: To keep the end papers and rods dry while the hair is wrapped
To keep the lotion warm so that it works on the hair faster
The chemicals can irritate the skin and cause rashes
To stop the wet hair from slipping off the rods while wrapping

questions.stem: What is put around the hairline before the waving lotion is applied?
options: Barrier cream and a strip of cotton wool to protect the skin
Hair gel to hold the short baby hairs flat against the skin
Hairspray, so that the lotion does not run down the face
Conditioner, so that the lotion works faster around the edges

questions.stem: Waving lotion splashes into a client's eye. What should you do first?
options: Wipe the eye with a dry towel to soak up the lotion
Put a few drops of neutraliser in the eye to stop the lotion
Rinse the eye at once with plenty of clean, cool running water
Finish the perm quickly, then check the eye once the rods are out

questions.stem: Why should the perm area be well ventilated?
options: To dry the hair faster while it is still wound on the rods
To keep the lotion cool so it works more slowly
To clear the strong fumes from the lotion and neutraliser
To stop the client from feeling the heat of the dryer

questions.stem: How should perm lotions and neutralisers be stored?
options: In a cool, dry place out of sunlight, closed tight and labelled
On a sunny window shelf so that they stay warm and ready to use
Poured into spare spray bottles with no labels, for much quicker use
Mixed together in one large bottle to save space on the shelf

questions.stem: What is the main job of end papers when wrapping a perm?
options: To hold the rod firmly in place against the head
To soak up the extra neutraliser from the hair ends
To protect the scalp and skin from the waving lotion
To keep the ends smooth and stop bent 'fish hook' ends

questions.stem: How does the size of the perm rod affect the curl?
options: A smaller rod gives a tighter, smaller curl
A larger rod gives a tighter, smaller curl
Rod size only changes how long the perm lasts
Rod size makes no difference to the curl

questions.stem: Why should metal bowls, clips or combs not be used with perm chemicals?
options: Metal tools are too heavy to hold wet hair in place
Metal makes the lotion thicker and much harder to apply evenly
Metal tools are hard to clean after a chemical service
Metal can react with the chemicals and spoil the result

questions.stem: Which wrap divides the head into nine panels, with the rods in straight rows inside each panel?
options: A spiral wrap
A bricklay wrap
A piggyback wrap
A basic wrap

questions.stem: Why might you choose a bricklay wrap?
options: It uses fewer rods, so the service is cheaper and quicker
It stops gaps (splits) showing between rows of curls
It makes the curl much tighter at the ends than at the root
It needs no end papers or protective cream

questions.stem: Which wrap is best for long hair, to give an even curl from the root to the ends?
options: A basic wrap on very small rods
A wrap with the hair ends left out of the rods
A spiral wrap along the length of the rod
A wrap using only the very largest rods

questions.stem: What does 'on-base' placement of a perm rod mean?
options: The rod sits fully below its section, resting on the skin
The rod sits halfway off its section, for a little lift
The rod is wound with no tension at all
The rod sits on its own section, giving most root lift

questions.stem: How much tension should you use when winding hair round a perm rod?
options: As tight as you can, so the curl lasts longer
Even and firm, without stretching the hair
Very loose, so the hair hangs off the rod
Tight at the root and loose at the ends

questions.stem: Why must the rubber band of a rod not press hard into the hair at the root?
options: It can mark or break the hair along the band line
It makes the lotion work more slowly on the ends
It stops the neutraliser from reaching the scalp
It makes the curl turn in the wrong direction

questions.stem: How should the hair be shampooed before a perm, unless the maker says otherwise?
options: With a hard scalp massage to open up the pores
With a rich conditioner left in the hair to protect it
Gently, without rubbing or scratching the scalp
Twice with hot water, to swell the hair shaft

questions.stem: After the waving lotion is rinsed out, why is the hair blotted well with a towel?
options: To dry the curl into place before the rods come out
So the neutraliser is not watered down by extra water
To rub the lotion deeper into the hair before rinsing
To cool the scalp so the client is more comfortable

questions.stem: How long should the waving lotion be left on the hair?
options: Always 45 minutes, whatever the hair type or texture
Until the client's scalp starts to tingle
Until the hair on the rods feels completely dry to the touch
For the time the maker says, checked with test curls

questions.stem: During processing, how do you take a test curl to check the perm?
options: Take out every rod at once and look at the curl on the whole head
Unwind a rod 1½ turns, ease it in and look for an 'S' shape
Pull a wet strand off the rod and see how fast it springs back
Press each rod with your fingers to feel whether the hair is soft

questions.stem: What is likely to happen if a perm is over-processed?
options: The curl will be loose because the lotion was too weak
The hair may be weak, frizzy and hard to comb
The hair will be shinier and stronger than it was before
The curl will be tighter, with the hair in perfect condition

questions.stem: When the maker says to, a plastic cap is put over the rods during processing. Why?
options: To stop the client from touching or moving the rods
To keep the neutraliser from drying out on the ends
To protect the plastic rods from the dryer's heat
To keep in body heat and stop the lotion drying out

questions.stem: After processing, how should the waving lotion be rinsed out?
options: Just a few seconds, so that the new curl is not washed out
Thoroughly, for the time the maker says, with the rods in
Not at all, because the neutraliser goes straight on top
Only once all the rods have been taken out of the hair

questions.stem: How should the neutraliser be applied?
options: To the dry hair after the rods are removed
Evenly over every rod, for the time the maker says
Only to the rods at the crown, where the hair is thickest
Mixed into the waving lotion before the perm starts

questions.stem: Why must the rods be taken out gently after neutralising?
options: To keep the end papers in good shape for the next client
Because the rods are still very hot from the waving lotion
Because the curl is still soft and can be pulled out of shape
So that more of the neutraliser stays inside the rods for longer

questions.stem: What is a curl reformation (soft curl perm) on very curly or coily natural hair?
options: A perm that only adds a rich colour to the hair while it curls it
A temporary set made only with water, setting lotion and rollers
A two-step perm that softens the natural curl, then winds it on rods
A treatment that makes the hair grow out of the scalp in a looser curl

questions.stem: In a curl reformation, what is the first product (the rearranger or softener) used for?
options: To loosen the tight natural curl so it can be wound on rods
To fix the new curl in place so that it will not drop out later
To moisturise the finished curls each day after the service is done
To clean the scalp and hair thoroughly before the service starts

questions.stem: After a curl reformation, why is daily moisturising usually advised?
options: To make the new curl get tighter and tighter each day
To wash the last of the perm chemicals out of the hair
Because the treated hair can dry out and break easily
To stop the hair colour from fading in the hot sun

questions.stem: What should you tell a client about washing her hair after a perm?
options: Wait as long as the maker advises before the first shampoo
Shampoo it the same evening to take away the chemical smell
Shampoo it twice a day for the first week to keep it fresh
Never shampoo it again until the perm has fully grown out

questions.stem: Which advice helps a permed client keep her curls?
options: Use a moisturising conditioner and avoid hard brushing
Brush the curls hard every day with a fine bristle brush
Use a hot flat iron each day to smooth out the curls
Tie the hair up tightly in a bun while it is still wet

questions.stem: Why should you check the whole head when the rods are out and the hair is rinsed?
options: To count the rods and end papers for the stock sheet
To check the curl is even and the scalp is not irritated
To decide how much more to charge the client for the service
To see whether the client would like a hair colour as well

questions.stem: How should perm rods be dealt with between clients?
options: Wiped with a dry towel and put straight back into the rod tray
Kept in a bag for the same client and never cleaned at all
Washed clean, then disinfected and dried as the Centre says
Left soaking in the sink in a little of the waving lotion

questions.stem: What is the difference between cleaning and disinfecting a tool?
options: Cleaning removes dirt and hair; disinfecting then kills most germs
Cleaning kills all germs; disinfecting only removes hair
They are the same thing, done with different cloths
Disinfecting is done first, then cleaning removes the disinfectant

questions.stem: Why should the perm details be written on the client's record card?
options: So that the salon can charge the client more at the next visit
Because the client must sign it before each and every visit
So that the stylist can claim the service as her own work
So the next stylist knows the lotion, rods, timing and results

questions.stem: How should leftover perm lotion in a bowl be dealt with?
options: Poured back into the bottle for the next client
Thrown away as the maker and the Centre's rules say
Kept in an open bowl on the trolley for later
Mixed with neutraliser and kept for the next perm

questions.stem: During the perm, the client says her scalp is burning. What should you do?
options: Rinse the lotion off the area at once and tell the instructor
Tell her that burning is normal and leave the lotion on the hair
Put her under a hot dryer so that the perm finishes much sooner
Give her a cool drink and leave the lotion on until the time is up

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Name the oxidising chemical found in most perm neutralisers.
What is the name of the chemical change in which the waving lotion breaks the disulphide bonds?
What is the name of the chemical change in which the neutraliser re-forms the bonds?
Is the pH of an alkaline waving lotion above or below 7?
What word describes the hair's ability to stretch and go back to its length without breaking?
Many makers ask for a skin test a set time before a chemical service. How many hours is this most often?
What test is done on a few cut strands to check whether chemicals already on the hair (such as metallic dyes) will react with perm products?
What is the name of the skin condition, with redness, itching and cracking, that can come from handling perm chemicals without gloves?
What comb, with a long thin handle, is used to make clean partings for perm sections?
What is the name of the plastic tool that the hair is wound round to make a perm curl?
What is the name of the rod placement where the rod sits completely below its section, giving the least lift at the root?
What is the name of the wrap for long hair in which two rods are used on one strand, one on the mid-lengths and one on the ends?
In a curl reformation, what is the second product, applied after the hair is wound on rods, that puts the curl into the hair?
What waterproof cover is put over the client's clothes before a chemical service?
What kind of comb should a client use on her new curls, so that she does not pull them straight?

essays.stem: Describe the checks you would make during a consultation before giving a client a perm.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would ask the client what result she wants and show her pictures, so we agree on the size and shape of curl. I would ask about her past chemical services, such as relaxers, colour, henna or home dyes, and when they were done, and about allergies and any medical conditions. I would look at the scalp for cuts, sores, redness or signs of infection; if I found any, I would not perm and would advise her to see a doctor. Then I would check the hair: its texture (fine, medium or coarse), its density, its porosity and its elasticity, and its length, because these decide the lotion, the rods and the timing. I would do a skin test, an incompatibility test and a test curl when the maker requires them. Last, I would write everything on her record card and agree the price and time.
markingPoints: Asks about the result wanted and agrees it with the client
Asks about past chemical services, allergies and medical conditions
Checks the scalp for cuts, sores or infection, and does not perm (refers) if found
Checks hair texture, density, porosity, elasticity and length
Does the skin, incompatibility and test-curl checks the maker requires, and records them

essays.stem: Explain in simple words how a perm changes straight or loose hair into curly hair.
essays.modelAnswer: Inside each hair are strong links called disulphide bonds, which hold the hair in its natural shape. First the hair is wound on rods, which give the new shape. The waving lotion is alkaline, so it swells the hair and lifts the cuticle, and then it breaks some of the disulphide bonds. This is called reduction. With the bonds broken, the hair softens and takes the shape of the rod. When the test curl shows the right 'S' shape, the lotion is rinsed out well. Then the neutraliser, which is usually hydrogen peroxide, is put on. It re-joins the bonds in their new place. This is called oxidation. The hair now holds the curl, even after it is washed, until it grows out or is cut off.
markingPoints: Hair shape is held by disulphide bonds inside the hair
The rods give the new shape
The waving lotion swells the hair and breaks the bonds (reduction)
The lotion is rinsed out when the test curl is right
The neutraliser re-forms the bonds in the new shape (oxidation), so the curl is permanent

essays.stem: Describe how you would protect yourself and your client from harm during a perm service.
essays.modelAnswer: Before I start, I check the client's scalp for cuts or irritation and check that any skin test the maker requires was done and was clear. I put a cape and towels on the client, and a strip of cotton wool and barrier cream around the hairline and ears. I wear gloves and an apron whenever I touch the lotion or neutraliser. I work in a well-ventilated area to clear the fumes. I read the maker's instructions and follow them exactly, I never mix products from different makers, and I keep the lotion away from the eyes. If lotion gets in an eye, I rinse it at once with plenty of clean water and get help. If the client feels burning, I rinse the area straight away and tell the instructor. I wipe up spills at once so nobody slips.
markingPoints: Checks the scalp and the skin test result first
Protects the client: cape, towels, cotton wool and barrier cream
Wears gloves and an apron; works with good ventilation
Follows the maker's instructions; never mixes brands
Knows first aid for eyes and skin, and stops and reports if the client feels burning

essays.stem: Describe the steps for winding one perm rod neatly and correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: I take a section that is no longer than the rod and no wider than its diameter, using the tail comb to make clean, straight partings. I comb the section smooth from root to ends and keep it damp. I hold the hair at the angle I need for the base control I want; for on-base I hold it straight out from the head. I fold an end paper over the ends so that all the ends are covered and none are bent. I place the rod under the ends and wind the hair down towards the scalp smoothly, with even, firm tension but without stretching the hair. I stop at the base and fasten the band across the top of the rod, so it does not press into the hair at the root. Then I check that the ends are smooth and the rod sits on its base.
markingPoints: Section matches the rod's length and diameter, with clean partings
Hair combed smooth and held at the angle for the base control wanted
End paper covers the ends with no bent ends (fish hooks)
Winds smoothly with even, firm tension, without stretching
Band fastened so it does not press into or mark the hair

essays.stem: Explain how and why you take test curls while a perm is processing, and what you do with the result.
essays.modelAnswer: Test curls show me when the hair has taken enough curl, so that the perm is not under-processed or over-processed. I start checking at the time the maker says. I take test curls on different parts of the head, such as the front, the crown and the nape, because the hair may process at different speeds. I put on gloves, undo the band and carefully unwind the rod about 1½ turns, holding the hair so that it does not come loose. I ease the hair towards the scalp and look at the shape. If it makes a firm 'S' shape that matches the rod size, processing is finished and I rinse at once. If the curl is weak, I wind it back and check again a few minutes later, but I never go past the maker's longest time. I note the time on the record card.
markingPoints: Reason: to stop the perm being under- or over-processed
Checks from the time the maker says, in several areas of the head
Unwinds about 1½ turns carefully, wearing gloves
A firm 'S' shape matching the rod means ready: rinse at once
If weak, rewinds and rechecks, never going past the maker's time; records it

essays.stem: Describe the steps from the end of processing to the removal of the rods.
essays.modelAnswer: When the test curls are ready, I take the client to the basin and rinse the lotion out with lukewarm water, with the rods still in, for as long as the maker says. I rinse gently so that I do not disturb the rods, and I protect the client's face and eyes with a towel. Then I blot every rod well with a towel, because extra water would weaken the neutraliser. I put fresh cotton wool around the hairline if needed. I apply the neutraliser slowly and evenly to every rod, top and underneath, and leave it for the time the maker says. Then I take the rods out gently, without pulling or stretching the curl, and apply the rest of the neutraliser if the maker says to. Last, I rinse, and use a light conditioner if the maker allows it.
markingPoints: Rinses thoroughly with lukewarm water, rods in, for the maker's time
Blots the rods well so the neutraliser is not watered down
Applies neutraliser evenly to every rod and times it as the maker says
Removes the rods gently without pulling the curl
Rinses and finishes as the maker says (second neutraliser, light conditioner)

essays.stem: Describe the main steps of a curl reformation (soft curl perm) on very curly natural hair, and the aftercare you would advise.
essays.modelAnswer: A curl reformation changes tight, coily hair into a looser, larger curl. First I consult, check the scalp, and do the skin and strand tests the maker requires. I check that the hair has no hydroxide relaxer on it. Wearing gloves, I apply the rearranger (softener) cream, comb it through gently and leave it for the time the maker says, until the natural curl has loosened. I rinse it out well and blot. Then I wind the hair on rods of the size chosen, with end papers. I apply the booster lotion to every rod and process it, taking test curls. I rinse, blot, apply the neutraliser and time it, then remove the rods gently. For aftercare I advise a curl moisturiser every day, a wide-tooth comb or pick, sleeping on a satin scarf or bonnet, and regular salon conditioning treatments.
markingPoints: Consults and does the skin and strand tests; checks there is no hydroxide relaxer
Applies and times the rearranger to loosen the natural curl, then rinses
Winds on rods and applies the booster, with test curls
Rinses, blots and neutralises as the maker says
Aftercare: daily moisturiser, wide-tooth comb or pick, satin scarf, conditioning

essays.stem: Explain how you would clean up the work area and store the products after a perm service.
essays.modelAnswer: When the service is finished, I wear gloves to clean up. I close every bottle tightly and wipe the outside, then put the products back in the store room in a cool, dry place out of sunlight, with their labels facing out. I throw away any lotion or neutraliser that is left in a bowl or applicator, as the maker and the Centre's rules say; I never pour it back into the bottle. Used end papers, cotton wool and neck strips go in the bin. I wash the rods, bowls and combs to remove all chemicals and hair, then disinfect and dry them. Used towels and capes go in the laundry, and I wipe the trolley, chair and basin. I sweep up hair and mop any spills so nobody slips. Last, I write the products used on the stock sheet and the record card.
markingPoints: Closes, wipes and stores products in a cool, dry place out of sunlight, labelled
Throws away leftover lotion as the maker and Centre say, never back in the bottle
Washes, then disinfects and dries rods, bowls and combs
Bins single-use items; sends towels and capes to the laundry; wipes surfaces
Sweeps, mops spills, and records stock used

essays.stem: Compare an under-processed perm with an over-processed perm: what each looks like, the likely causes, and how to prevent them.
essays.modelAnswer: An under-processed perm has a weak, loose curl that may drop out within a few days, because not enough bonds were broken. Likely causes are taking the lotion off too soon, a lotion too weak for the hair, too little lotion, or rods that were too large. An over-processed perm has hair that feels weak, dry and frizzy, is hard to comb, and may even break, because too many bonds were broken. Likely causes are leaving the lotion on too long, a lotion too strong for porous or tinted hair, or not taking test curls. Both faults are prevented the same way: do a full hair analysis, choose the right lotion and rod size, follow the maker's timing, take test curls often, and rinse at once when the curl is ready.
markingPoints: Under-processed: weak or loose curl that drops
Under-processed causes: too short a time, weak lotion, too little lotion, large rods
Over-processed: weak, dry, frizzy hair that is hard to comb or breaks
Over-processed causes: too long a time, lotion too strong for porous or tinted hair, no test curls
Prevention: hair analysis, right lotion and rods, maker's timing, regular test curls

essays.stem: What aftercare advice would you give a client after a perm, and why should the service be written on her record card?
essays.modelAnswer: I would tell the client to wait as long as the maker advises before the first shampoo, so the curl can settle. She should use a gentle shampoo and a moisturising conditioner made for chemically treated hair, and comb from the ends upwards with a wide-tooth comb instead of brushing hard. She should avoid tight hair bands, too much heat from irons, and swimming in pools or the sea without rinsing after. Sleeping on a satin scarf or pillowcase helps to keep the curls. I would suggest a follow-up visit for a trim and treatment. The record card should show the date, the results of the tests, the lotion used, the rod sizes, the wrap, the processing time and the result. This helps the next stylist repeat a good result or avoid a problem, and it shows the salon followed the right steps.
markingPoints: Wait before the first shampoo as the maker advises
Gentle shampoo, moisturising conditioner, wide-tooth comb, no hard brushing
Avoid too much heat and tight bands; rinse after swimming; satin scarf
Record card shows tests, lotion, rods, wrap, time and result
Reason: repeat good results, avoid problems, and show correct steps were followed

practical1.title: Water wrap: basic and bricklay perm wraps on practice heads
practical1.brief: As a group, set up a clean perm workstation and wrap two practice (mannequin) heads with damp hair, using water only and no chemicals. One head is wrapped in a basic (nine-section) wrap and the other in a bricklay wrap. First, section the basic head together into nine panels, and agree who wraps which panel. Every member wraps at least one panel on the basic head and at least six rods on the bricklay head, while the assessor watches. Each member must use end papers, keep even tension, and place the band so it does not press on the root. Photograph each stage below (hair and rods only) and add the photos to the group's practical. When both heads are finished, clean and disinfect the rods and combs, and hand in once for the whole group.
materials: 2 practice heads with hair at least 10 cm long, on clamps
Perm rods in several sizes, with bands
Capes and towels for the practice heads
Disinfectant for tools, as the Centre uses
photos: The workstation set up, with tools clean and laid out
The basic head sectioned into nine panels
Close-up of one member placing an end paper and starting a wind
The finished basic wrap from the front, top and back
The finished bricklay wrap from the top and back
The rods and combs washed and in the disinfectant, and the area clean
checklist: Made clean, straight partings with sections that match the rod size
Combed the hair smooth and kept it damp while wrapping
Used end papers correctly, with no bent ends (fish hooks)
Wound with even, firm tension and placed each rod on its base
Fastened the band so it does not press into or mark the hair
Followed the wrap pattern (straight rows or bricklay) without gaps
Cleaned, disinfected and put away tools, and left the area tidy
safety: Keep the floor dry; wipe up water at once so nobody slips
Hold the tail comb pointing away from your face and others
Clamp the practice heads firmly so they cannot fall
Stand with a straight back and take short breaks to rest your arms

practical2.title: Full permanent wave service on a model or human-hair practice head
practical2.brief: As a group, give a complete perm service on a model who agrees to it, or on a practice head with human hair, from consultation to finish. A model must have had any skin test the maker requires, done the time ahead that the maker says, with a clear result. A model with very curly natural hair is given a curl reformation instead, as the instructor directs. Share the work: one member leads the consultation and fills in the record card; one does the strand and test-curl checks and the gowning and barrier cream; all members wind at least one panel each; one times the processing and takes test curls; one rinses, neutralises and removes the rods; and one finishes and gives aftercare advice. Swap so that each member also helps with another stage. Follow the maker's instructions exactly. Photograph each stage below, showing the hair and rods only, never the model's face unless the model agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group with the record card.
materials: A model who agrees, or a practice head with human hair
Perm lotion and neutraliser from the same maker, suited to the hair
Perm rods, bands and end papers
Gloves, aprons, capes, towels and neck strips
Tail combs and wide-tooth combs, plastic clips
photos: The completed record card and skin test note (no names showing if the model prefers)
The hair sectioned and the barrier cream and cotton wool in place
The full head wound on rods
A test curl showing the 'S' shape
The neutraliser being applied to the rods
The finished curl, dried and styled, from the back and side
The workstation cleaned, with products closed and stored
checklist: Took part in the consultation and checked the scalp for contraindications
Wore gloves and an apron, and protected the client with cape, towels and barrier cream
Wound a panel neatly with end papers and even tension
Applied lotion and neutraliser evenly, timed as the maker says
Took test curls correctly and rinsed at the right time
